Republic of the Philippines DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT DILG-NAPOLCOM Center, EDSA corner Quezon Avenue, West Triangle, Quezon City http: //wwu.dilg.com.ph DILG OPINION No. 147 s. 2022 November 15, 2022 DIR. JUAN JOVIAN E. INGENIERO Regional Director, DILG Region VI P. Aquino St., Fort San Pedro Iloilo City Dear RD Ingeniero: This refers to your Memorandum dated 19 October 2022 echoing the following queries of Hon. Karl J. Silverio, Sangguniang Kabataan Municipal Federation (SKMF) Vice president of the Municipality of San Miguel, Iloilo, quoted herein in toto: ii. v. vi. vii. As SKMF Vice President, do I need to prepare my Notice of Assumption to Office personally and present the said document to their office (Sangguniang Bayan of San Miguel)? Considering that based on DILG 6's reply that there is a temporarily vacant position in the Office of the Ex-Officio member, who will declare the position vacant, an official or a document? Is there a need for an administrative complaint for the position to be declared vacant? What documents should be submitted to the Office of the Sangguniang Bayan before I could be recognized to temporarily assume the position of Acting SKMF President? Is it the responsibility of the MLGOO to file a complaint against the absences of Mr. Tadifa? Who shall effect my assumption to the office? Do I need an official directive to officially and legally assume office? Per representation, on 3 October 2022, the Criminal Investigation and Detention Group (CIDG) Iloilo CFU Personnel led by PMAJ Jess Baylon implemented Search Warrant No. 01-2002 against Mikhail Khali S. Tadifa, SKMF President of the Municipality of San Miguel, Iloilo for violation of RA No. 10951 or the Comprehensive Firearms and Ammunitions Regulation Act. Since the SKMF President is now detained in the Municipal Police Station Detention Cell, as correctly pointed out by Regional Office 6, there arises temporary vacancy. Hence, the above mentioned queries. In addition thereto, your good Office also posted these questions, for additional guidance: 1. Whether the instances which give rise to a temporary vacancy in the Office of the Pederasyon President are limited to: (1) a suspension as a result of an administrative case; and (2) has taken any form of authorized leave of absence either as a Pederasyon President or an ex-officio member Of the Sangguniang Panlungsod/Bayan or Panlalawigan; and "Matino, Mahusay at Maasahan" Trunkline No.: 8876-34-54

2. Whether Mr. Tadifa is compelled to file a leave of absence given his arrest and subsequent detention so as not to incur an absence without leave that will result in a permanent vacancy in the office. At the outset, the Central Office agrees with the discussions of your Office on the first issue. The instances when the position of Federation President is considered temporarily vacant shall not be limited to the grounds laid down in Section 41(b)1 of DILG-NYC-COMELEC Joint Memorandum Circular No. 2017-012. It must be emphasized that the President of the Pambayang Pederasyon ng mga Sangguniang Kabataan is also member, albeit ex-officio, of the Sangguniang Bayan3, thus, temporary vacancy as defined under the Local Government Code of 1991 (LGC) equally applies to him. There arises temporary vacancy if the official is temporarily incapacitated to perform his duties for physical or legal reasons such as, but not limitéd to, leave of absence, travel abroad, and suspension from office4. With respect to the second issue, we answer in the negative. Mr. Tadifa may not file a leave of absence given his arrest and subsequent detention. The case of Miranda vs. the Hon. Sandiganbayan, et.a15 is enlightening, thus: "xxx First. Section 13 of R.A. No. 3019, as amended, provides: Section 13. Suspension and loss of benefits. — Any incumbent public officer against whom any criminal prosecution under a valid information under this Act or under Title 7, Book II of the Revised Penal Code or for any offense involving fraud upon government or public funds or property whether as a simple or as a complex offense and in whatever stage of execution and mode of participation, is pending in court, shall be suspended from office. Should he be convicted by final judgment, he shall lose all retirement or gratuity benefits under any law, but if he is acquitted, he shall be entitled to reinstatement and to the salaries and benefits which he failed to receive during suspension, unless in the meantime administrative proceedings have been filed against him. In the event that such convicted officer, who may have already been separated from the service, has already received such benefits he shall be liable to restitute the same to the Govemment. The Sandiganbayan properly construed Section 13 of R.A. No. 3019 as covering two types of offenses: (1) any offense involving fraud on the govemment; and (2) any offense involving public funds or property. xxx xxx In a Resolution dated 4 February 2002, the Sandiganbayan preventively suspended Mayor Miranda from office for 90 days. The anti- graft coun held that a violation of Article 177 of the RPC involves fraud "which in a general sense is deemed to comprise anything calculated to deceive, including all acts, omissions, and concealment involving 1 In case the Pederasyon President is suspended as a result of an administrative case or has taken any form of authorized leave of absence either as a Pederasyon President or an ex-officio member Of the Sangguniang Panlungsod/Bayan or Panlalawigan for more than one month, the Vice president Of the Pederasyon shall..xxx 2 Entitled, GUIDELINES ON THE CONDUCT OF SANGGUNIANG KABATAAN (SK) PEDERASYON ELECTION; AND RULES GOVERNING TERMS OF OFFICE, SUSPENSION AND REMOVAL OF ALL SK PEDERASYON OFFICERS 3 Section 446 of the Local Government Code of 1991 4 section 46, LGC 5 G.R. No. 154098 dated July 27, 2005 Page 2 of 3

a breach of legal or equitable duty, trust or confidencejustly reposed, resulting in damage to another or by which an undue and unconscious advantage is taken of another. It further ruled that Miranda's act fell within the catch-all provision "x x x or for any offense involving fraud upon govemment. Xxx" Thus, suspension as mentioned above from public office during the trial shall not be considered as penalty. It is not a penalty because it is not imposed as a result of judicial proceedings. In fact, if acquitted, the official concerned shall be entitled to reinstatement and to the salaries and benefits which he failed to receive during suspension6. Hence, filing of leave of absence is not necessary. Going now to the queries of Hon. Silverio, we will address the same in one discussion as the questions propounded are related. With this, it may be prudent to clarify that under Section 41(b)(I) of of DILG-NYC- COMELEC JMC No. 2017-01, when the the Pederasyon President is suspended due to legal reasons, as in this case, the Vice President of the Pederasyon shall automatically assume the office of the concerned Pederasyon President in an acting capacity until such time that the concerned Pederasyon President reassumes his/her office. Correspondingly, he shall automatically exercise the powers and perform the duties and functions appurtenant to the office. The phrase "automatically exercise" means that upon the happening of the situation or incident that temporarily incapacitates the Concerned pederasyon president (e.g. leave of absence, travel abroad, suspension from office, and the like), the pederasyon vice-president assumes as acting president and there is no need for the issuance of another document before he can exercise the powers and perform the duties and functions of the pederasyon president. Needless to state therefore that there is •no need for Hon. Silverio to prepare Notice of Assumption and any other documents before he could be recognized to temporarily assume the position as Acting Pederasyon President. Neither is there a need to declare the position vacant nor an administrative complaint to be filed for the position to be declared vacant. Thus, an official directive to officially and legally assume the office is not necessary. Notwithstanding, this opinion is being issued without prejudice to any contrary opinion, decisions, and orders of more competent authorities and/or the courts. We hope to have assisted you accordingly. Thank you. Very. truly yours, Authority of the Secretary: A ICTOR R.
